misconceptions.description: Submitting a mockup, document, or screenshots as if it were a published site instead of a real committed file tree at a live URL
misconceptions.trigger: learner delivers a docx or screenshots rather than the actual published repo
misconceptions.feedback: The deliverable is a real file tree committed to username.github.io and served at a live URL. A mockup or document is not a published site.

misconceptions.description: Treating one module skill (for example visual polish) as standing in for the full set of accessibility, privacy, and publishing checks
misconceptions.trigger: learner polishes appearance but omits alt text, privacy review, or a verified live URL
misconceptions.feedback: The studio integrates accessibility, privacy, and publishing. Show all three: alt text, no committed secrets, and a working live URL you verified.

misconceptions.description: Omitting any note of where AI assisted, leaving the work's honesty and the learner's ownership unclear
misconceptions.trigger: learner used AI for drafting or debugging but includes no AI-use note
misconceptions.feedback: Add a short AI-use note: where AI helped, that you verified the output, and that you own the final decisions. Disclosure keeps the work honest.

misconceptions.description: Judging the project by hours spent or commit count rather than by an end-to-end test of the live site
misconceptions.trigger: learner submits without loading the live URL on another device to confirm it works
misconceptions.feedback: Effort is not evidence the site works. Run one end-to-end check on the live URL from a phone, confirming load, alt text, links, and no exposed secrets.
